label: Run command
description: Run a command in one of the computer's shell sessions, as its user (who may use sudo), with the screen as its display, so a window it opens shows on the screen. `args` is `{ command, restart, timeoutSecs }`. A session keeps its folder and its exported variables from one command to the next, so a `cd` or an `export` carries over (a plain variable, a readonly one or a function does not); it runs one command at a time, and one sent while another runs fails, naming it, while different sessions run side by side. `session` names it: left out, the computer's default session; a name that does not exist yet starts a new session in the home folder. Nothing stays open between commands, so a session costs nothing while it waits; EndSession stops what its commands left running and forgets it. `restart: true` ends the session first (alone, without a command, it only does that). `timeoutSecs` stops the command, and everything it started, after that many seconds (optional; left out, it runs until it ends). A command that does not end by itself (a server, a watcher) is started in the background with `&`, or it holds its session. A long command parks the run while it goes, holding no worker. The whole output comes out as a file, however long: to show it to a model, pass it through TextPreview. A command that exits non-zero still succeeds here: its exit code is on `exitCode`.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: The `computer` output of the Computer node to act on.

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: The command, in the shape the node's description gives. RouteComputerCall's `command` port hands it over from a model's tool call; written by hand, it is a record literal.

inputs.name: session
inputs.label: Session
inputs.description: Which session to run in: a name you choose, which keeps its own folder and variables. The default agent names its session after the run's id (GetRunId), plus its `agentId` when that is set, so agents running at once keep apart; a name that outlives the run (one per agent you call again later) keeps its folder between runs. Left out, the computer's default session.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The command's whole output, standard output and standard error together, as a text file stored for this run (wire it through KeepFile to keep it longer).

outputs.name: exitCode
outputs.description: The command's exit code: 0 when it succeeded.

metadataPorts.name: tools
metadataPorts.description: The tools a model calls this node through, in Anthropic's names and in OpenAI's: gather them up to the LLM node's `tools` through metadata ports.

anthropic.description: Run a command in the computer's shell (bash) and get back its output and its exit code. Your shell keeps its folder and exported variables from one command to the next, so cd and export carry over; commands run one at a time. A long output comes back cut to its start and its end, with a line saying how much was cut: to read another part, run the command again through grep, head, tail or sed -n, or, for a command not safe to run twice, send its output to a file first (cmd > out.txt 2>&1) and read the file in parts. A command that does not end by itself (a server, a watcher) must be started in the background with & and its output sent to a file, or it holds the shell and every later command waits. Windows a command opens appear on the screen. Prefer a command to the mouse and keyboard for anything a command can do.
anthropic.name: bash

restart.description: true starts your shell over first, in the home folder, stopping whatever it runs and whatever its commands left running. Alone, without a command, it only restarts.

timeout_secs.description: Stop the command after this many seconds. Left out, it runs until it ends.
